text:
Priya Raman: pushed a sweep run this morning comparing batcher window strategies across regions + GPU families. focused on continuous coalescing vs strict split. models: mosaic-13b-8k (q4f16) and m13b (q2b). GPUs: H100 (us-west), A100 (eu-west), A10G (ap-south). windows: [2ms, 8ms, 20ms, 50ms], max_batch_tokens: [512, 1024, 2048]. fairness tilt on/off. link to dashboards: https://console.internal.redwood/batch/sweeps/1913123456 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Sahil Gupta: nice. do you have p50/p95 token latency and throughput per-region? curious about the 50ms window behavior on h100.

Priya Raman: yep, summary in the dashboard. quick highlights: on H100 coalesce (continuous) with 8ms window + max_batch_tokens 1024 gave best cost/latency tradeoff for p95 end-to-end (text-gen mode). 50ms raised tail on APAC due to much larger microburst coalescing with long prompts. A100 showed less benefit from coalesce vs strict split because cutlass kernels saturated earlier.

Anya Lee: can you paste the config you ran? want to reproduce the 8ms + 1024 setting.

Priya Raman: sure

Priya Raman: ```
# batcher config snippet
batcher:
  mode: continuous_coalesce
  window_ms: 8
  max_batch_tokens: 1024
  jitter_ms: 1.5
  fairness_tilt: 0.2  # 0..1, higher favors low-latency tenants
  kv_cache_policy: prefix_cache
kernels:
  selection: auto  # flashattn-v2 preferred on H100
  force_cutlass: false
```

Devon Carter: interesting about fairness_tilt. did you try 0 vs 0.5? how bad were the long-tail tenants when tilt=0?

Priya Raman: tilt=0 (pure throughput) improved aggregate tokens/sec by ~9% but p95 for small-tenants jumped ~2.2x on eu-west during peak. tilt=0.5 brought p95 down close to baseline with only ~3% throughput loss.

bench-bot: summary (aggregated across runs):
```
model | gpu  | window | max_tok | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | tokens/s | cost/unit
m13b  | H100 | 8ms    | 1024    | 18      | 86      | 12.1     | $0.024
m13b  | A100 | 8ms    | 1024    | 22      | 110     | 9.6      | $0.032
m13b  | A10G | 20ms   | 2048    | 35      | 220     | 7.3      | $0.018
mosaic | H100| 8ms    | 1024    | 25      | 120     | 10.4     | $0.028
```

Priya Raman: also ran kernel sweeps. on H100 flash-attn-v2 wins for seq_len<=1024, but for long sequences cutlass-backed custom fused-gemm gave more stable tail. quant routes (q2b vs q4f16) had tiny quality diffs (0.4-0.8% eval delta) but q2b saved ~18% token-cost on A100.

Sahil Gupta: is the cost calc including idle batch fill overhead? and how did you measure tokens/s (inflight vs completed)?

Priya Raman: cost includes GPU time + kernel overhead. tokens/s measured as completed output tokens/sec per GPU aggregated across the job window. idle fill was counted separately — coalesce reduced idle fill by ~6% on H100 during steady traffic.

Anya Lee: any regression on output quality when we force coalesce + q2b? we saw weird repetition in a prior run.

Priya Raman: we ran eval suite (1000 prompts) — small uptick in repetition F1 on q2b+coalesce for few-shot prompts but within alert thresholds. flagging to research for model-onboard checklist.

Devon Carter: can we add an automated guard in the rollout to backoff coalesce if repetition score crosses X? I'd prefer that before enabling coalesce by default for Dedicated customers.

Priya Raman: agreed. plan: rollout policy -> enable continuous_coalesce with tilt=0.2, and eval-gate on new quant/model combos. if eval diff > 1% on repetition metric, auto-fallback to split mode for that customer.

deploy-bot: experiment 1913123456 -> rollout rule created (canary 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%)

Sahil Gupta: thanks. can you drop the raw logs/artifacts in the sweep folder? I want the kernel traces and per-socket GPU timelines.

Priya Raman: uploading now to S3 path: s3://redwood-bench/eng-ml/sweeps/1913123456/bench-outputs.tar.gz

bench-bot: note: next run suggestion: try window_ms=5 with jitter_ms=2 on ap-south to tame the microburst tail.

Priya Raman: noted, scheduling follow-up run tomorrow AM. will share a short write-up with recommended defaults for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Anya Lee: nice work, this is actionable. :rocket:

Sahil Gupta: +1 — want to include a short blurb in docs about kernel choices per seq_len/gpu.

Priya Raman: will draft it. thanks all! :slightly_smiling_face:
